```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "Payer and price are stronger. A sells to finance/ops leads with a business budget. Live competitor pricing runs from $29-99/mo (NeverFined) and $49/mo or $490/yr (ExpirationOps) up to $500-800/location/yr (ClearBot). B sells to financially strained individuals at $8-24/mo, and free alternatives (GapZero) are already live.",
    "Retention fits the model better. License renewals, audits and rule changes recur, which suits a monthly subscription. B's own brief says the need is largely one-time and ends at re-employment, which caps lifetime value.",
    "Acquisition economics look less hostile for A. Its $10-13 CPC is cost per click, not per customer, so it does not directly compare with B's $62-118 Google cost per lead. But each A customer is worth more, so A can absorb acquisition costs that would sink B's $8-24/mo price, which B's brief itself flags as a problem.",
    "Risk exposure is lower. A can follow the 'tracking only, not legal advice' posture that competitors already use. B handles sensitive health, caregiving and disability data and gives career-trajectory advice, which raises the risk of harm and GDPR/CCPA burden for a one-person operation.",
    "Both ideas are crowded, but A's competitors show that paying B2B customers exist at multiple tiers. B's competitors include free tools and a pre-alpha entrant, and two have unpublished or NOT FOUND pricing. That makes B's evidence of willingness to pay weaker."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "The every.to quote ('I don't have $100–$150 per hour to spend on a career coach... but I do have a subscription to ChatGPT') is offered as demand evidence. It actually shows the target user turning to a general-purpose AI they already pay for rather than buying a dedicated tool, so it undercuts willingness to pay for B. B's pricing evidence is also partly missing: ResAlign's price is unpublished and CoachGPT's pricing is NOT FOUND.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate confidence. A has real weaknesses. It has at least seven competitors already running the same SEO playbook. It has no clear wedge against $29-49/mo trackers. The ~$14.50 RegTech CPC is unsourced. Retention on cheap trackers is unknown. Data maintenance across all 50 states is a burden the brief admits a six-week build likely can't meet. A wins mainly because B's unit economics and one-time need look structurally worse, not because A's evidence is strong."
}
```
